item.title: Russia willing to resume peace talks with Ukraine, US after Witkoff visit
item.description:
Russian President Vladimir Putin told White House envoy Steve Witkoff on Wednesday that he "agrees in principle" resuming trilateral peace talks between Russia, Ukraine and the U.S. to end the war, the Kremlin said. Why it matters: The White House hopes Putin will show more willingness to compromise after President Trump agreed to lift sanctions on Russian diesel sales and took other steps welcomed by Moscow. For now, it seems the only concession Putin agreed to is to negotiate. Driving the news: During a three-hour meeting in St. Petersburg, Witkoff presented Putin with an updated proposal to end the war in Ukraine . Trump envoy Jared Kushner joined virtually. Before the meeting, Russia released U.S. citizen Stephen Hubbard, 74, who had spent more than four years in captivity after being seized by Russian troops in eastern Ukraine in April 2022. item.title: Nigeria confirms Ebola case linked to East Africa
item.description:
Case in Africa’s most populous country was detected in a woman who had travelled from Uganda Nigeria has confirmed an Ebola case in its capital, Abuja, after a woman who arrived from Uganda tested positive for the virus, the health ministry said. The woman began showing symptoms on 7 October and was admitted to a hospital in Abuja four days later, where she was later diagnosed with Ebola. It is unclear when she arrived in Nigeria, Africa’s most populous country. Continue reading...

item.title: Trump’s crackdown on immigrant voting in California is a ploy to influence election
item.description:
The federal crackdown on voting by non-citizens in California is obviously aimed more at having a political impact than combating serious crime. It bolsters President Donald Trump’s repetitive, but unproven, claims that Democrats have stacked the political deck by allowing non-citizens to vote. It singles out California, a deeply blue state and a whipping boy in elections across the nation. Finally, it occurs as Californians are marking mail-in ballots for the Nov. 3 midterm election and deciding the fate of Proposition 39 , which would require voters to show eligibility credentials. Last week, Trump’s Justice Department sued California and Los Angeles County , after demanding that state officials set aside ballots from 20,000 registered voters it says may not be eligible to vote. item.title: Epstein’s attorney and accountant accused of ‘facilitating and concealing’ his crimes in lawsuit
item.description:
New Mexico lawsuit claims ‘in exchange for furthering Epstein’s criminal project, his associates received generous salaries’ The attorney general of New Mexico on Wednesday filed a civil lawsuit against Jeffrey Epstein’s longtime attorney, Darren Indyke, and Epstein’s longtime accountant, Richard Kahn, accusing them of having “facilitated and concealed” Epstein’s crimes, and is seeking to stop them from being paid by Epstein’s estate while the litigation plays out. The lawsuit , filed in the US district court for the district of New Mexico, names Kahn and Indyke as defendants both in their individual capacity, and in their capacity as co-executors of Epstein’s estate. The complaint also names Epstein’s estate, and the 1953 Trust, which holds the estate’s assets. Continue reading...

item.title: Raids at far-right group's offices at European Parliament
item.description:
President Emmanuel Macron announced France would receive an additional 200,000 tonnes in monthly diesel deliveries from the Gulf during his tour of the region Tuesday, as the Élysée attempts to quell spiraling cost-of-living protests. Grievances fueled by high gas prices exploded into rioting across France this week, prompting Paris to deploy troops ahead of planned demonstrations Saturday. Rising fuel costs have boosted the political fortunes of French far-right leader Marine Le Pen, who has “ owned ” the issue for “quite some time,” an expert told Reuters. The crunch has energized Europe’s rightist parties who are pressuring governments in Germany, Italy, and Poland to restore energy ties with Russia: “I love the smell of Russian gas in the morning,” a Polish far-right leader said. — Brendan Ruberry

item.title: Texas data center boom could erase decades of progress on air quality
item.description:
A group of Texans believe they’ve discovered evidence that the state’s environmental regulatory agency has continued to issue permits to data centers despite Governor Greg Abbott’s call for it to stop. The nonprofits Public Citizen and FracTracker Alliance, working with local activists in Texas, looked through the public database of the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ) and discovered that the organization has worked on multiple permits for data center projects since Abbott called for a pause in the process on September 21. Abbott’s office denied approving any new permits in a statement to 404 Media. According to Public Citizen and the FracTracker Alliance, which cite documents publicly available on the TCEQ’s website, the agency has reviewed documents and assigned engineers related to more than a dozen permits related to data center projects in the state. item.title: Thousands of California public employees begin strike over contract
item.description:
A tablet at the counter of the Department of Motor Vehicles in Fresno on Oct. 2, 2026. Photo by Larry Valenzuela for CalMatters Perhaps today is not the best day to go to the DMV. California state workers are planning a one-day strike today in multiple cities including Sacramento, San Francisco and Los Angeles. They’re protesting what they say are unfair labor practices by Gov. Gavin Newsom’s administration. The work stoppage could affect services at the DMV, unemployment offices and other departments. SEIU Local 1000 represents about 100,000 workers employed in dozens of agencies across the state. They’re accountants, government analysts, nurses, IT workers, custodians and more.
